name: Assa
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Assa is the original name of the goddess Nessa, who is also spelled Ness and Nes. Nessa is remembered as the mother of the great king Concobar mac Nessa. The name Assa means "gentle one." Her father, Eochaid, was the king of Ulster. He raised Nessa in dignity and comfort, and she studied under twelve tutors. The druid Cathbad killed all twelve tutors in one night to reach her. Nessa took up arms, gathered warriors, and set out to find the killer and take revenge. From this violent turn she gained the name Nessa, meaning "ungentle." She later bore a son whose name, Concobar mac Nessa, means "son of Nessa." Some legends say the child was conceived when Cathbad forced himself on her, while others say Nessa conceived through magic. The entry for Assa directs the reader to the fuller article on Nessa.

okr.objective: Establish Assa as the original gentle-one name of the goddess Nessa, mother of Concobar mac Nessa.
